title: Check: monitoring and logs
description: Five questions on keeping evidence after the fact.

questions.prompt: Why aggregate logs off the node?

options.text: Container logs disappear with the Pod, and rotate on the node

questions.explanation: Post-mortems happen after the Pod is gone. If the logs were only on the node, the evidence went with it.

questions.prompt: What shape does a log shipper usually take?

options.text: A DaemonSet, one Pod per node
A sidecar in every Pod, always

questions.explanation: One agent per node reads every container's log files. A sidecar is the fallback for an app that will not log to stdout.

questions.prompt: metrics-server versus Prometheus - what is the split?

options.text: metrics-server serves current usage for kubectl top and the HPA; Prometheus stores history and alerts

questions.explanation: Asking metrics-server for last week's data is a category error - it keeps nothing.

options.text: They are the only source of Pod logs
They explain scheduling, image and probe failures, and expire after about an hour

questions.explanation: The single most useful record of why something did not start - and it evaporates.

questions.prompt: Which signals give the quickest read on cluster health?

options.text: Node conditions, Pod restarts and pending Pods

questions.explanation: Nodes not Ready, Pods restarting and Pods stuck Pending cover most of what goes wrong.
